message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that depends on a handful of variables—crew size, equipment, weather, and the exact scope of work (primer only, full repaint, restoration, etc.). In practice, the tower’s maintenance schedule gives us a useful benchmark:

| What’s being done | Typical duration |
|-------------------|------------------|
| **Full repaint** (cleaning, primer, top‑coat) | ~2 years (in practice, the work is staged over two years, but the actual “on‑site” painting time is closer to 6–12 months). |
| **Primer only** | ~6 months |
| **Top‑coat only** | ~3–4 months |

Why the difference? The tower’s 324 m height and 18,000+ rivets mean that crews can’t work continuously at all levels. They usually paint in sections, moving from one platform to the next, and they have to wait for suitable weather conditions. Safety protocols also slow things down – workers are lowered in harnesses, and the tower’s iron structure needs careful handling to avoid corrosion.

So, if you’re asking how long it would take a dedicated crew to paint the whole thing from start to finish, you’re looking at roughly **six to twelve months of active work**, spread out over a couple of years in reality.
